answer: Every newcomer enters hollow, with no credit and no right to earn until it passes three unannounced gale audits, each run by a randomly drawn panel of strangers who never audit the same applicant twice. Its entry stake sits in a glacier vault that thaws one slice per passed audit, so a fake cannot cash out early. If an audit exposes shared code, funding, or operator fingerprints, the whole stake is burned, approving auditors lose their own bonds, and the required lock doubles for the next applicant from that fingerprint cluster, so running n clones costs far more than n times one honest lock.
